# Autopsy of a Dead Project

Note: the full submission narrative is the published DEV post (that body is the real description):
https://dev.to/dmustapha/i-built-a-coroner-for-dead-software-it-issues-death-certificates-and-it-refuses-to-lie-2o07

## Short description
A forensic pathology tool for software. Paste a GitHub URL and a machine examines the body, says what the project was, works out how it died, and issues a death certificate: cause of death, time since the last sign of life, a differential diagnosis, and the project's recovered last words. Alive repos get a certificate of life.

Two open-weight models do the work. TabPFN (Prior Labs tabular foundation model, run locally) returns the verdict as a posterior over six death modes from a 10-feature GitHub vector. deepseek-v4.1-flash on 0G Compute reads the evidence, breaks the closest calls, and writes the eulogy. A grounding gate refuses any generated line that does not trace to the real README or commit record, so the tool would rather say "I could not ground this" than invent a death it cannot defend.

On a held-out test (leave-one-out over 117 hand-labelled repos), TabPFN scores 58.1% against a 1-nearest-neighbour baseline at 43.6%, a 14.5 point gap, which is the whole argument for a foundation model over a lookup table.

Open weights end to end. The verdict comes from weights you can inspect, run offline, pin to a version, and call for free. No closed oracle decides how your project died.

## Theme
Día de los Muertos: remember the dead by name, with a cause of death the tool can defend. Not fear, memory.
